review.brief: Review RM2-tesla-add-charging-history (tesla adapter, Tier 1). Boundaries (stateless adapter, no DB, no HTML, only test-fake stubs outside tesla), conventions (...Tesla suffix, milesToKm N/A confirmed not skipped, nullable *float64), correctness (Option A pagination termination, RFC3339 parse, 401->ErrUnauthorized/403->ErrForbidden), tests (offline httptest only, no Raw*/live call, cost isolation), spec/tasks coverage + no weakening, read-heavy profile. Review the diff at 494cb35 + 991475a. Escalate on doubt.

findings.note: StartTime/EndTime query params appended without url.QueryEscape (vehicles.go). Pre-existing package pattern but newly reachable (first string query params in the package); an RFC3339 '+' offset would decode as space. Not exercised yet — no caller passes date filters; auto-pagination uses numeric pageNo only. Fix belongs to Tier 2 when it wires date-range backfill.

decisions.decision: Pagination = Option A: ChargingHistory auto-fetches all pages internally (offset pageNo/count) and returns the merged history; ChargingHistoryParams.PageNo!=0 is a single-page escape hatch.
decisions.why: RM2 tier-1 scope mandates 'pagination-aware' and Tier 2 backfills the full history; pagination belongs inside the adapter (anti-corruption boundary). Write-side/nightly call, not a hot read path. Approves worker DES6 recommendation over Option B.

decisions.decision: Extended T6 to stub ChargingHistory on the telemetry fakeTesla too, not just the gateway one named in tasks.md.
decisions.why: Adding ChargingHistory to VehicleService broke every test double implementing the port; the telemetry fake (service_test.go) was a second implementer the worker did not flag. Both are cross-module test-only compile fixes owned by the leader.

decisions.decision: Accepted review finding R1 (unescaped StartTime/EndTime query params) but DEFERRED the fix to Tier 2, which is the first code to actually pass those date-range params (backfill). Did not reopen the reviewer-approved code for a currently-unreachable path.
decisions.why: The auto-pagination path uses only numeric pageNo (safe); no caller passes date filters yet. Fixing now would force a re-review round for zero runtime effect. Recorded on Tier 2's roadmap notes so it is not lost.
